claims.summary: generate_dialogue (L763) assembles a multi-tiered prompt with a gradual-fade history compression (L836-853): older exchanges progressively truncated to fit context.
claims.disposition: Verified at the report-bound SHA. L763 is the async generate_dialogue signature; L836-891 build alternating user/assistant history via attended_history_limit/attended_history_trim_len, oldest short to newest full. The L844 comment names gemma-3-4b-it 8k; the live profile per witness is gemma4_12b (16k canary) so that comment is historical, not a runtime claim.

claims.summary: user_content_budget (L893-900) subtracts committed overhead (system prompt + history) from assembly_prompt_budget_chars.
claims.disposition: Verified exactly. L896 overhead = sum of messages[*].content.len(); L898-900 user_content_budget = assembly_prompt_budget_chars.saturating_sub(overhead).saturating_sub(100).

claims.summary: Content is organized into PromptBlock structures (L914-970) with priorities and char caps (journal_cap, direct_cap, ambient_cap) modulated by the attention variable.
claims.disposition: Verified. L914-995 build 11 PromptBlocks; caps come from attended_journal_caps/attended_perception_caps/attended_web_cap/etc (prompt_contracts.rs L147-202), which return compiled constants when attention is None and scale by the ATTEND ratios otherwise.

claims.summary: user_content_budget can reach 0: if overhead + 100 exceeds assembly_prompt_budget_chars the double saturating_sub floors at 0.
claims.disposition: Verified. The chained saturating_sub (L898-900) does floor at 0 under enough overhead. This is the intended saturating floor, not UB; her observation that the value CAN be 0 is exactly correct and is the antecedent her Test 1 / Suggested Next asks to pin.

claims.summary: If assemble_within_budget (L904) does not handle a zero budget by prioritizing critical blocks (topline/spectral), the model could get an empty or severely truncated prompt and produce incoherent output.
claims.disposition: Graceful handling verified: at budget 0 the min_chars floors keep prefixes of journal(700)/direct_perception(900)/topline(360)/agenda(320), and the caller always appends 'Fill X%.' + turn_instruction + the system prompt, so the prompt is never empty. Contradiction preserved: she named spectral as protected, but spectral has min_chars 0 and is fully evicted at budget 0 despite sharing priority 3 with topline. Protection is keyed on min_chars, not priority.

claims.summary: Budget Exhaustion Test: verify user_content_budget hits 0 and assemble_within_budget still includes a priority-3 block (topline/spectral) over lower-priority blocks.
claims.disposition: Implemented her test at the exact target layer. New prompt_budget.rs regression zero_budget_keeps_protected_floors_and_is_never_empty exercises assemble_within_budget with budget 0 and the real dialogue block shape: journal/topline/agenda retain their floors, output is non-empty, and topline(pri 3, min 360) survives while spectral(pri 3, min 0) is evicted. Passes.

claims.disposition: Behavior verified in source: L862 minime_excerpt = chars().take(trim_len).collect(); L875-880 strips lines whose trimmed start is 'NEXT:' before the char take. A dedicated unit test needs a testable seam extracted from the inline async generate_dialogue (being-facing dialogue-assembly code); I deliberately do not refactor that in this non-live headless run. claims.summary: Suggested Next: verify the priority-based selection inside assemble_within_budget handles user_content_budget == 0 gracefully.
claims.disposition: Answered. Source analysis shows the zero-budget path retains the min_chars floors and never empties the prompt, and the new regression pins it. The one honest correction: 'gracefully' does not mean every named-critical block survives — spectral (min_chars 0) does not. Whether spectral should get a floor is a being-facing prompt-assembly design change (Tier 5); not made here.
